display.purpose: Hero headlines only. Maximum typographic impact, minimum weight. Serif family per niche.

headline.purpose: Section titles on the landing page. Steps down from display in scale but maintains serif authority.

body.purpose: All reading text, forms, CRM content. Neutral sans, always. Capped at 65ch for readability.

label.purpose: Status badges, stat labels, metadata. Uppercase, wide-tracked, small but assertive.

shadows.name: elevated-light-default
shadows.purpose: Default light mode card elevation. Neutral, structural, diffuse.

shadows.name: elevated-dark-default
shadows.purpose: Default dark mode. Deep void with subtle top-edge highlight.

shadows.name: elevated-tattoo-dark
shadows.purpose: Tattoo dark: hard, minimal. The 1px wire is the only relief.

shadows.name: elevated-nails-light
shadows.purpose: Nails light: mauve-tinted, pillowy, generous spread.

shadows.name: elevated-estetica-light
shadows.purpose: Estetica light: barely-there warmth. Clinical cleanliness.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Card entrances, page transitions. Fast start, gentle settle.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover states, focus rings. Instant feedback.

motion.name: duration-normal
motion.purpose: Card transitions, theme switches, surface changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main CTA across booking wizard and landing page. Uppercase, bold, wide-tracked.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #d97706; color: #fafafa; padding: 16px 32px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; border: none; border-radius: 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #f59e0b; color: #09090b; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.95); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d97706; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary actions: cancel, back, dismiss. Transparent with accent text.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #d97706; padding: 12px 24px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; border: 1px solid #e4e4e7; border-radius: 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #f4f4f5; border-color: #d97706; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d97706; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Glass Card Interactive

components.html:
Classic Haircut

Precision cut tailored to your style.

narrative.overview:
A single structural system that completely transforms its visual identity for each business niche. The stage (layout, components, interactions) stays architecturally consistent; the set design (colors, typography, radius, shadows, photography) changes so dramatically that two deployments feel like entirely different products. The transformation is not cosmetic. Each niche carries its own atmosphere, its own weight, its own way of handling light and depth.

The system rejects the template look. If a visitor could see a barbershop deployment next to a nail salon deployment and think "same template," the transformation has failed. Equally, if a developer could look at the admin panel and think "generic SaaS dashboard," the product side has failed. The CRM is not a backoffice; it is the daily instrument of a business owner standing behind a counter with a phone in one hand.
keyCharacteristics: Niche-driven shapeshifting: every visual property adapts per niche
Dark/light per context, not per preference
CRM density optimized for phone-behind-the-counter usage
RTL-native: Hebrew and English receive equal structural attention
Zero visual debt: no inherited SaaS conventions

rules.name: The Niche Owns Its Palette Rule
rules.body: Every deployment has exactly one accent hue. That hue comes from the niche preset or the client's branding, never from a generic 'primary blue.' The token --brand-accent is the single source of truth.

rules.name: The Status Is Sacred Rule
rules.body: Status colors (emerald success, red error, amber warning) are constant across all niches. They never change. Business-critical signals are not styled by the niche.

rules.name: The Niche Owns Its Voice Rule
rules.body: Font families change completely per niche. A tattoo deployment should feel typographically alien to a nails deployment. The hierarchy ratios stay consistent; the families swap.

rules.name: The Admin Stays Neutral Rule
rules.body: The CRM/admin panel always uses the body sans (Inter or niche equivalent). Decorative display faces never appear in the admin.

rules.name: The Niche Casts Its Own Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadow values are never shared across niches. Each niche's shadow-elevated carries the hue and character of its physical space.

dos: Do let the niche transform everything: color, type, radius, shadow, motion.
Do use the token architecture (--brand-accent, --brand-accent-light, --brand-surface-dark) as the single source of truth.
Do test every component in all five niches AND both light/dark modes before shipping.
Do keep CRM interactions under 2 taps for common tasks.
Do respect the physical scene per niche.
Do use semantic status classes instead of raw color utilities.
donts: Don't build generic SaaS dashboard layouts with identical card grids.
Don't create cookie-cutter layouts that look like Wix or Squarespace service pages.
Don't over-animate the landing page. Motion serves booking conversion, not spectacle.
Don't let the admin panel feel like a spreadsheet.
Don't use #000000 or #ffffff. Every neutral carries a niche tint.
Don't apply decorative display fonts in the CRM/admin.
Don't use border-left/right > 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't use glassmorphism as a decorative default.
Don't build hero-metric cards (big number, small label, gradient accent).
